items.title: Audit the operator-brief layer against BRF-101 before the next run executes anything
items.hypothesis: The instruction layer has carried at least one more concept-where-members-belong defect than the packet enumeration -- BRF-101's class predicts recurrence anywhere a brief compresses a protocol list ('same discipline', 'as before', 'per HANDOFF').
items.discriminatingTest: For each recurring brief phrase that compresses a list, locate the enumeration of record it stands for and verify it exists as a committed, citable artifact; any phrase with no enumeration behind it is a BRF-101 instance. 'Same discipline' is the obvious first candidate: it currently expands only via precedent in context, exactly the mechanism that decayed.
items.whyItMatters: The evidenced cause of the only silent artifact loss in the program was a brief, not a run. Checking the runs while leaving the briefs unchecked repairs the symptom layer only.
items.wouldChangeWhat: Whether future briefs are executable as received or flagged defective before execution, per the standing BRF-101 requirement.
items.cost: one short audit; enumerations-of-record for any naked concepts found (the packet's already exists: tests/test_closing_packets.py REQUIRED)

items.title: Extend the packet check to content-shape, not only presence
items.hypothesis: The current test verifies presence and non-emptiness; a run could still ship a structurally hollow required artifact (valid JSON, no items; a report of one line). Schema-level checks (backlog has items or an explicit empty-with-reason field; manifest has the required keys) close the next-cheapest evasion of the enumeration.
items.discriminatingTest: A deliberately hollow artifact planted in a scratch run directory fails the extended check; all seven real closed runs pass it.
items.whyItMatters: PKT-101's own history: this run's opening commit shipped an empty PROMPT.txt placeholder -- the presence check alone would have blessed it before the non-empty clause was added. Shape is the next rung of the same ladder.
